claims.quote: There's an official CLI app for Linux.
claims.statement: The project has an official CLI application that runs on Linux.

claims.quote: It's maintained by me
claims.statement: The official CLI app is maintained by the seller (the author).

claims.quote: even though I cannot promise to provide proper support
claims.statement: The seller does not promise proper support for the CLI app.

claims.quote: The instructions below describe how to use all the features using `curl`.
claims.statement: This document's instructions cover all of the product's features, usable via curl.

claims.quote: The application can be used from the terminal using something like `curl`.
claims.statement: The service can be operated from a terminal using curl.

claims.quote:
You can get the version of `chhoto-url` the server is running using `curl http://localhost:4567/api/version` and
get the siteurl using `curl http://localhost:4567/api/siteurl`.
claims.statement: The server implements an /api/version route and an /api/siteurl route that respond to requests.

claims.quote: These routes are accessible without any authentication.
claims.statement: The /api/version and /api/siteurl routes require no authentication.

claims.quote: **This is required for programs that rely on a JSON response from Chhoto URL.**
claims.statement: Programs that rely on JSON responses from the service must use API key validation.

claims.quote: In order to use API key validation, set the [`CHHOTO_API_KEY`](./INSTALLATION.md#chhoto_api_key) environment variable.
claims.statement: API key validation is enabled by setting the CHHOTO_API_KEY environment variable.

claims.quote: If this is not set, the API will default to cookie validation (see section above).
claims.statement: When CHHOTO_API_KEY is not set, the API defaults to cookie validation.

claims.quote:
If the API key is insecure, a warning will be outputted along with a generated
API key which may be used.
claims.statement: The server checks whether the configured API key is insecure and, if so, generates a usable replacement key and emits a warning message.

claims.quote: **All responses for requests using API key are JSON encoded.**
claims.statement: The server serializes its responses to API-key-authenticated requests as JSON.

claims.quote: For each response, the response code will be `200`, `401`, `400`, `500`, or `404`, depending on the context.
claims.statement: The server's request handlers and error paths are written to return only the status codes 200, 401, 400, 500 and 404, selecting among them by context.

claims.quote: Some of the requests/responses use `shorturl` and `longurl`, while some use `shortlink` and `longlink`.
claims.statement: The API names the short and long URL fields inconsistently: some requests and responses use shorturl/longurl and others use shortlink/longlink.

claims.quote: I don't want to change it since it might break compatibility, and the issue isn't big enough to make that worth it.
claims.statement: The seller does not intend to change the API's field naming, because changing it might break compatibility.

claims.quote:
curl -X POST \
    -H "X-API-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
    -d '{ \
        "shortlink":"<shortlink>", \
        "longlink":"<longlink>", \
        "expiry_delay": <expiry_delay>, \
        "notes": "<notes>" \
        }' \
    http://localhost:4567/api/new
claims.statement: Links are added by sending a POST request to the /api/new endpoint.

claims.quote: -H "X-API-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
claims.statement: Requests to the API are authenticated by an X-API-Key header carrying the caller's API key.

claims.quote:
-d '{ \
        "shortlink":"<shortlink>", \
        "longlink":"<longlink>", \
        "expiry_delay": <expiry_delay>, \
        "notes": "<notes>" \
        }' \
claims.statement: The link-creation request body accepts the fields shortlink, longlink, expiry_delay and notes.

claims.quote: If `<shortlink>` is empty or omitted, one will be generated automatically.
claims.statement: If the shortlink field is empty or omitted, the server generates a short link automatically.

claims.quote: The `<expiry_delay>` is specified in seconds.
claims.statement: The expiry_delay parameter is interpreted as a number of seconds.

claims.quote: It is capped to a maximum of 5 years.
claims.statement: The expiry_delay value is capped at a maximum of 5 years.

claims.quote: A missing `<expiry_delay>` or a value of 0 will disable expiry.
claims.statement: Omitting expiry_delay or setting it to 0 disables expiry for the created link.
A successful creation request is answered with a JSON object containing the fields success, error, shorturl and expiry_time.
A failed request is answered with a JSON object containing the fields success, error and reason.

claims.quote: Multiple links can be created in a single request by sending an array of objects like the example below.
claims.statement: The target's creation endpoint accepts a request body that is an array of link objects and contains code that creates a link for each object in the array.

claims.quote: In that case, the response is an array containing one result per input object (in order), each in one of the formats shown above.
claims.statement: For a batch creation request, the server responds with an array holding one result per input object, in the same order as the inputs, each in one of the documented response formats.

claims.quote: Except for malformed requests or internal server errors, the HTTP status code is always `200`.
claims.statement: The target's request handling returns HTTP status 200 for responses other than malformed-request rejections and internal server errors, indicating failure through the body's success field instead of the status code.

claims.quote:
curl -H "X-API-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
-d '<shortlink>' http://localhost:4567/api/getconfig
claims.statement: The server exposes a `/api/getconfig` endpoint which, given a shortlink and an API key, returns the configuration for that backend.

claims.quote: (This would work without authentication in public mode.)
claims.statement: In public mode, the `/api/getconfig` endpoint works without authentication.

claims.quote:
{
    "version": "<version>",
    "site_url": "<site_url>",
    "allow_capital_letters": true/false,
    "public_mode": true/false,
    "public_mode_expiry_delay": "<delay>",
    "slug_style": "<style>",
    "slug_length": "<len>",
    "try_longer_slug": true/false
}
claims.statement: A successful `/api/getconfig` reply is a JSON object with the fields version, site_url, allow_capital_letters, public_mode, public_mode_expiry_delay, slug_style, slug_length and try_longer_slug.
A failed `/api/getconfig` reply is a JSON object with success false, error true, and a reason field.

claims.quote: curl -H "X-API-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>" http://localhost:4567/api/whoami
claims.statement: The server exposes a `/api/whoami` endpoint which, given an API key, returns the current user's role.

claims.quote:
The server will reply with `admin` if admin access is granted, `public` if admin access is not granted but public mode is enabled,
and `nobody` if no access is granted.
claims.statement: The `/api/whoami` reply is `admin` when admin access is granted, `public` when admin access is not granted but public mode is enabled, and `nobody` when no access is granted.

claims.quote:
curl -X PUT \
-H "X-API-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
-d '{ \
    "shortlink":"<shortlink>", \
    "longlink":"<longlink>", \
    "reset_hits": <bool>, \
    "expiry_time": <time>, \
    "notes": <notes> \
    }' \
http://localhost:4567/api/edit
claims.statement: The server exposes a `/api/edit` endpoint which edits an existing short link, accepting shortlink, longlink, reset_hits, expiry_time and notes, and requiring an API key.

claims.quote: The fields `expiry_time` and `notes` are optional.
claims.statement: In an `/api/edit` request, the expiry_time and notes fields are optional.

claims.quote: The existing values will be kept in the database if nothing is provided.
claims.statement: When optional `/api/edit` fields are not provided, the existing values for them are kept in the database.
An `/api/edit` reply is a JSON object with success, error and reason fields.

claims.quote:
curl -H "X-API-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
-d '<shortlink>' http://localhost:4567/api/expand
claims.statement: The target exposes an /api/expand endpoint that accepts an API key header and a shortlink in the request body and contains a handler that looks up that shortlink and returns its stored information.

claims.quote:
{
    "success": true,
    "error": false,
    "longurl": "<longurl>",
    "hits": "<hits>",
    "expiry_time": <expiry_time>,
    "notes": "<notes>"
}
claims.statement: A successful /api/expand reply is JSON containing the fields success, error, longurl, hits, expiry_time and notes.
A failed /api/expand reply is JSON containing success set to false, error set to true, and a reason field.

claims.quote: (This route is not accessible using cookie validation.)
claims.statement: The /api/expand route cannot be accessed using cookie validation, only API key validation.

claims.quote: curl -H "X-API-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>" http://localhost:4567/api/all
claims.statement: The target exposes an /api/all endpoint that accepts an API key header and contains a handler that gathers the currently available links and returns them as a list.

claims.quote:
`page_after`: An offset where to start pagination after. It should be a valid shortlink, or an empty response will be received.
   This is faster, and the preferred way of doing pagination.
claims.statement: /api/all supports a page_after parameter that paginates starting after a given offset, which must be a valid shortlink or an empty response is returned; it is the faster, preferred pagination method.

claims.quote: `page_size`: The size of a returned page in number of shortlinks. Default value is 10.
claims.statement: /api/all supports a page_size parameter giving the number of shortlinks per page, whose default value is 10.

claims.quote: `page_no`: Alternative way of doing pagination. This is slower, and should be used only when using `page_after` isn't viable.
claims.statement: /api/all supports a page_no parameter as an alternative, slower pagination method, to be used only when page_after is not viable.

claims.quote: `filter`: For filtering links. The filter is applied on `shorturl`, `longurl`, and `notes` fields.
claims.statement: /api/all supports a filter parameter, and the filter is applied on the shorturl, longurl and notes fields.

claims.quote:
Must be ASCII, and at least 3
   characters long.
claims.statement: The filter parameter must be ASCII and at least 3 characters long.

claims.quote: Only alphanumeric characters are used for the filtering. Everything else is treated as a separator.
claims.statement: Only alphanumeric characters take part in filtering; every other character in the filter is treated as a separator.

claims.quote: None of the parameters are required. In absence of all of those, all shortlinks are returned.
claims.statement: None of the /api/all query parameters are required, and when none are given all shortlinks are returned.

claims.quote: The entries should be positive integers.
claims.statement: The numeric /api/all parameter entries must be positive integers.

claims.quote: If only `page_size` is provided, the first page is returned.
claims.statement: When only page_size is provided to /api/all, the first page is returned.

claims.quote:
[
    ...
  {
    "shortlink": "<shortlink>",
    "longlink": "<longlink>",
    "hits": <hits>,
    "expiry_time": <expiry_time>,
    "notes": "<notes>"
  },
    ...
]
claims.statement: A successful /api/all reply is an array of entries, each containing the fields shortlink, longlink, hits, expiry_time and notes.

claims.quote: curl -X DELETE -H "X-API-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>" http://localhost:4567/api/del/<shortlink>
claims.statement: The target exposes a DELETE /api/del/{shortlink} endpoint that contains a handler which deletes the link named by the shortlink in the path (for example, `example` for `http://localhost:4567/example`).

claims.quote: The server will output when the instance is accessed over API, when an incorrect API key is received, etc.
claims.statement: The target contains output/logging code that is wired to print messages when the instance is accessed over the API and when an incorrect API key is received, among other events.

claims.quote: curl -X POST -d "<your-password>" -c cookie.txt http://localhost:4567/api/login
claims.statement: When a password is set up, POSTing the password to /api/login returns an authentication cookie that can be stored and reused.

claims.quote: You should receive "Correct password!" if the provided password was correct.
claims.statement: A correct password submitted to /api/login receives the response "Correct password!".

claims.quote:
For any subsequent
request, please add `-b cookie.txt` to provide authentication. Unless specified, all API methods should work with cookies.
claims.statement: Subsequent requests authenticate by presenting the stored cookie, and, unless specified otherwise, all API methods work with cookie authentication.

claims.quote:
If you do not define a [`CHHOTO_PASSWORD`](./INSTALLATION.md#chhoto_password) environment variable when starting the docker
image, authentication will be disabled.
claims.statement: If the CHHOTO_PASSWORD environment variable is not defined when starting the docker image, authentication is disabled.

claims.quote:
This if not recommended in actual use however, as it will allow anyone to create new links and delete
old ones.
claims.statement: With authentication disabled, the target's link-creation and link-deletion paths are coded to accept requests without requiring any credentials.

claims.quote: Since there are no logs, it's impossible to prove that those links aren't created by you.
claims.statement: The service keeps no logs.

claims.quote:
You can get the version of `chhoto-url` the server is running using `curl http://localhost:4567/api/version` and
get the siteurl using `curl http://localhost:4567/api/siteurl`.
claims.statement: A request to /api/version returns the version of chhoto-url the server is running, and a request to /api/siteurl returns the site URL.

claims.quote:
If the API key is insecure, a warning will be outputted along with a generated
API key which may be used.
claims.statement: When the configured API key is insecure, the server outputs a warning together with a generated API key that can be used.

claims.quote: **All responses for requests using API key are JSON encoded.**
claims.statement: Every response the server sends to a request authenticated with an API key is JSON-encoded.

claims.quote: For each response, the response code will be `200`, `401`, `400`, `500`, or `404`, depending on the context.
claims.statement: The response code the server actually sends for any request is one of 200, 401, 400, 500 and 404, chosen according to the context of the request.

claims.quote: Multiple links can be created in a single request by sending an array of objects like the example below.
claims.statement: A single request sent to the creation endpoint with an array of link objects results in multiple links being created.

claims.quote: Except for malformed requests or internal server errors, the HTTP status code is always `200`.
claims.statement: Apart from malformed requests and internal server errors, every response the running server sends carries HTTP status 200, with success determined only by reading the response body.

claims.quote:
curl -H "X-API-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
-d '<shortlink>' http://localhost:4567/api/expand
claims.statement: When /api/expand is called with an API key and a shortlink, it returns information about that single short link.

claims.quote: curl -H "X-API-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>" http://localhost:4567/api/all
claims.statement: Calling /api/all with an API key returns a list of all the currently available links.

claims.quote: curl -X DELETE -H "X-API-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>" http://localhost:4567/api/del/<shortlink>
claims.statement: Calling DELETE /api/del/{shortlink} deletes the named link, so it is removed from the service.

claims.quote: The server will output when the instance is accessed over API, when an incorrect API key is received, etc.
claims.statement: When the instance is accessed over the API, and when an incorrect API key is received, the server actually outputs messages, among other events.

claims.quote:
This if not recommended in actual use however, as it will allow anyone to create new links and delete
old ones.
claims.statement: When authentication is disabled, anyone, without authenticating, can create new links and delete old ones.
